claims.claim: Slack offboarding converts a departing user to Single-Channel Guest and changes their email to a personal address while leaving the account active in the workspace; because the org no longer controls that mailbox, the 'forgot my password' recovery path for the account now runs through an address the organization cannot audit or reclaim, meaning access recovery for a converted account is no longer verifiable by TTS admins.

The bug bounty policy states HackerOne is the only intake for vulnerability reports and there is no route to move a report filed elsewhere (email, public channel) into the program on the reporter's behalf, while the security-incidents policy directs staff to report suspicious activity/incidents (which could include a publicly-disclosed vulnerability) via email to itservicedesk@gsa.gov within 1 hour — creating two contradictory intake and audit paths for the same class of report, with no mechanism to reconcile which channel's record is authoritative.

Tock time entries made by the Tock team on behalf of an out-of-office employee are recorded identically to entries made by the employee themselves (no field distinguishes who submitted the entry), and the timekeeping manager's weekly review only confirms a timecard exists per person, not who filed it — so the audit trail for billable-hour attribution cannot distinguish self-reported time from third-party-entered time, undermining the timekeeping manager's stated verification role.
